q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(DISTINCT P.EMPLOYEE_ID), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 calculates the average experience years of all employees assigned to a project, while Q2 calculates the average experience years of unique employees assigned to a project.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 will give a higher average if an employee is assigned to multiple projects, as it sums up the experience years for each project and then divides by the number of projects. Q2 will give a lower average in this case, as it divides the total experience years by the number of unique employees, not the number of projects.
